items.fullText: 글로벌마켓 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 젠슨 황 딸 폭언까지 터졌다…"직원에 '금붕어' 호칭" 논란 입력 2026.11.19 18:02 수정 2026.11.19 19:26 지면 A10 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 손주형 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 엔비디아 '왕족 경영'의 민낯 매디슨 황, AI칩 밀반입 관여 의혹 막강한 사내 영향력에 불만 속출 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)의 장녀인 매디슨 황 엔비디아 수석이사 /사진=뉴스1 젠슨 황 전 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)의 사임을 불러온 ‘스파이 불륜 논란’이 그의 딸 매디슨 황과 사위 니코 카프레즈에게까지 번지고 있다. 이들이 대중국 반도체 밀수 의혹을 받는 싱가포르 기업 메가스피드 업무에 관여한 사실이 드러나면서다. 두 사람의 초고속 승진과 막강한 사내 영향력에 대한 내부 불만도 재조명되고 있다. 18일(현지시간) 파이낸셜타임스(FT)에 따르면 매디슨 황은 메가스피드와의 거래 의혹을 둘러싼 엔비디아의 대응 전략 수립에 깊이 관여한 것으로 파악됐다. 성추문 대응에 강점이 있는 홍보대행사 헬러를 지난해 봄 고용한 것도 매디슨 황인 것으로 알려졌다. 같은 해 가을에는 메가스피드 대응 관련 조직에서 최고위 홍보 임원 중 한 명을 업무에서 일시 배제하는 판단을 내렸다. 올해 9월 매디슨 황과 결혼한 카프레즈는 2024년 엔비디아에 입사해 메가스피드를 비롯한 아시아 지역 클라우드 협력업체를 관리했다. 그는 입사 1년여 만인 올해 1월 글로벌 인공지능(AI) 인프라 성장 담당 부사장으로 승진했다. 카프레즈와 매디슨 황은 런던비즈니스스쿨에서 공부하던 시절 만나 연인이 됐다. 엔비디아 이사회는 전직 미국 연방검사인 준 김에게 의뢰해 젠슨 황을 둘러싼 의혹에 관한 독립 조사를 벌이고 있다. 미국 상무부의 수출 통제 위반 가능성 조사와 별개로 이뤄지는 것이다. FT는 메가스피드와 엔비디아의 관계에 매디슨 황과 카프레즈가 연관돼 있다는 사실이 드러나면서 두 사람에 대한 감시가 더욱 강화될 것이라고 전망했다. 매디슨 황 부부가 구설에 오르자 엔비디아의 가족 경영 구조를 비판하는 목소리도 커지고 있다. 월스트리트저널(WSJ)에 따르면 엔비디아에서 근무한 한 관계자는 젠슨 황과 그의 자녀들이 회사에서 왕족처럼 대우받았다고 증언했다. 매디슨 황 부부는 자신들보다 직급이 높은 임원까지 비판했으며 가족 관계를 이용해 동료에게 영향력을 행사한 것으로 전해졌다. 일부 직원은 매디슨 황의 행동, 발언에 관해 인사 부서에 불만을 제기했다. 그는 무언가를 기억하지 못하는 직원을 ‘금붕어’라고 불렀다. 반면 다른 동료는 매디슨 황의 강압적 태도를 인정하면서도 회사 목표를 달성하기 위한 것이자 수평적인 조직 구조에서 비롯된 결과라고 옹호했다. 젠슨 황 사임 이후 직원들의 동요가 커지자 엔비디아는 직원 달래기에 나섰다. 콜렛 크레스 임시 CEO는 통상 이듬해 봄에 하던 임금 인상과 신규 주식 보상 일정을 오는 12월로 앞당기겠다고 발표했다. 손주형 기자 handbro@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 손주형 기자 손주형 기자는 한국경제에서 글로벌 경제 및 사회 이슈를 취재합니다. 최근에는 미국·이란 전쟁의 전황과 그 여파를 전달하고 있습니다. 토요일자 지면 코너에서는 테크(기술) 이슈를 중심으로 세계에서 벌어지는 흥미로운 소식을 소개합니다. 2024년 입사해 편집부와 건설부동산부를 거쳐 국제부에서 취재 중입니다. items.t: National security and AI figures urge DOJ to probe what Nvidia knew about chip smuggling
items.d: A letter from 15 national security and AI leaders scrutinized the chipmaker’s knowledge of illegal transfers of its chips to China.
items.fullText: EXCLUSIVE Artificial intelligence Artificial intelligence National security and AI figures urge DOJ to probe what Nvidia knew about chip smuggling A letter from 15 signatories scrutinized the chipmaker’s knowledge of illegal transfers of its chips to China. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 On Tuesday, Nvidia’s board of directors announced that it would establish a committee dedicated to investigating national security and export control compliance. David Paul Morris / Bloomberg via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 18, 2026, 10:00 AM EST By Jared Perlo A group of 15 national security experts and AI policy leaders is urging the Justice Department to investigate what Nvidia knew about the alleged smuggling of its advanced AI chips to China, and whether the company continued doing business with customers after evidence emerged that they were illegally diverting the technology. items.fullText: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now Systems from ASUS, Dell and MSI are now available — with more from Acer, GIGABYTE, HP and Microsoft on the way — bringing RTX acceleration and up to 128GB of unified memory to local AI, development and creative workflows. November 18, 2026 by Justin Walker 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 엔비디아 "투자 기업 엄격히 심사"…'AI 중앙은행' 역할 축소하나 입력 2026.11.18 18:14 수정 2026.11.19 09:22 지면 A5 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 김인엽 기자 구독하기 노유정 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 분기매출 1158억弗 '역대 최대'…홀로서기 본격화 구매약정 3900억弗로 40% 늘어 삼전닉스 수년치 HBM 일감 확보 젠슨 황 추진한 순환거래는 '제동' 네오클라우드 지원 까다로워질듯 한국경제신문의 투자 전문 유료 플랫폼 '한경 프리미엄9' 에 실린 기사입니다. 한경 프리미엄9 (www.hankyung.com/premium9) 을 구독하시면 더 많은 글로벌 투자 기사를 찾아볼 수 있습니다. 17일(현지시간) 콜렛 크레스 엔비디아 임시 최고경영자(CEO)가 CNBC ‘매드 머니’에 출연해 진행자 짐 크레이머와 젠슨 황 CEO 사임 이후의 경영 전략과 3분기 실적에 대해 이야기하고 있다. /CNBC 화면 캡처"> < 인터뷰 하는 크레스 임시 CEO > 17일(현지시간) 콜렛 크레스 엔비디아 임시 최고경영자(CEO)가 CNBC ‘매드 머니’에 출연해 진행자 짐 크레이머와 젠슨 황 CEO 사임 이후의 경영 전략과 3분기 실적에 대해 이야기하고 있다. /CNBC 화면 캡처 “젠슨 황은 떠났지만 인공지능(AI) 수요는 떠나지 않았다.” 17일(현지시간) 젠슨 황 없이 처음 이뤄진 엔비디아 분기 실적발표에 대한 기술 투자자 댄 아이브스의 평가다. 콜렛 크레스 임시 최고경영자(CEO)는 그간 젠슨 황이 추진한 인공지능(AI) 인프라 기업에 대한 순환거래(벤더파이낸싱) 축소를 시사하면서도 매출 증가율 예상치는 더 높였다. ‘가죽 재킷’을 벗은 엔비디아의 홀로서기가 본격화했다는 분석이 나온다. ◇젠슨 황 없이도 순항 이미지 크게보기 엔비디아는 이날 2027회계연도 3분기(2026년 8~10월) 시장 추정치를 웃도는 실적을 발표하면서 2028회계연도(2027년 2월~2028년 1월) 매출 증가율 전망을 전 분기 70%에서 75%로 상향 조정했다. 크레스 CEO는 “직전 분기 매출 증가율 추정이 70%로 제한된 이유가 공급망 한계 때문”이라며 “이번엔 고객에게 추가로 공급 가능한 물량을 반영했다”고 설명했다. 중국 데이터센터 매출은 포함되지 않은 수치다. 차세대 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 베라루빈의 출시 효과도 본격화했다. 기존 블랙웰을 잇는 AI 칩 베라루빈은 이번 분기에 본격 출하됐다. 크레스 CEO는 “베라루빈은 폭발적인 출발을 보이고 있다”며 “우리의 야심은 그 어느 때보다 크다”고 밝혔다. 베라루빈 등 제조에 필요한 부품 구매는 늘렸다. 엔비디아의 이번 분기 필수 부품·생산 역량 구매약정은 3900억달러로 전 분기(2790억달러)보다 40% 늘었다. 다년간의 메모리 장기공급계약(LTA)을 맺은 영향이다. 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스가 수년간의 HBM 일감을 상당 수준 확보했다는 해석이 나온다. 베라루빈에는 두 회사가 공급하는 HBM4(6세대)와 저전력 메모리 모듈인 ‘소캠(SOCAMM) 2’가 적용된다. 업계 관계자는 “젠슨 황 스캔들 등으로 최근 AI 투자 축소 우려가 불거졌지만 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 메모리를 원하는 기업은 여전히 많다”며 “대외 정책 불확실성으로 AI 투자 증가세가 일부 둔화할 가능성은 있지만 당분간 업황이 뒤바뀔 가능성은 크지 않다”고 내다봤다. 엔비디아의 다른 공급사도 한숨을 돌리게 됐다. 삼성전기는 엔비디아와 반도체 기판 관련 추가 계약을 맺었으며 엔비디아가 추가 자금 지원을 검토 중

items.t: Nvidia enters the post-Jensen Huang era with a bang
items.d: Nvidia delivered a message with its first earnings report under new leadership: The sky isn’t falling.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Nvidia enters the post-Jensen Huang era with a bang The company’s interim CEO delivered strong earnings and a clear message about the future of Nvidia without its charismatic former leader. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 NVIDIA says Jensen Huang will not return as CEO 01:47 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 17, 2026, 9:41 PM EST / Updated Nov. 17, 2026, 9:42 PM EST By David Ingram Nvidia delivered a message with its first earnings report under new leadership: The sky isn’t falling. With a new CEO and board chair just days after the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang, the company reported results Tuesday that beat analysts’ expectations for AI chip sales. Nvidia’s new leaders also appeared to calm some investors’ nerves about the immediate future of a company at the heart of the AI economy. Colette Kress, the interim CEO and Nvidia’s longtime chief financial officer, and Harvey Jones, the newly elected board chair, used the quarterly earnings call to answer many — but not all — of the biggest questions hanging over Nvidia, including who will be running things in the near term. Just hours before the earnings release, Huang had injected fresh uncertainty into precisely that question when announced that he would be “honored” to return to the job of CEO, if the company’s board decided to bring him back. At the top of Tuesday’s call, Jones shot down that idea . “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” he said. “While this was an unexpected transition, the board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company’s employees, customers, partners and shareholders.” Following the earnings call, Kress poured even more cold water on the idea of Huang’s return. “Jensen resigned from his position with Nvidia, and the board accepted his resignation,” she said in an interview with CNBC. “The board has determined that they will not reinstat

items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. items.fullText: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab November 16, 2026 by Allen Bourgoyne 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 16TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. The playbook for NVIDIA HPC SDK is coming soon, bringing GPU-accelerated C, C++ and Fortran compilers, libraries and message passing interface tools to the DGX Spark cluster — the same development tools used on NVIDIA-powered supercomputers. items.fullText: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future Over two decades running the most complex manufacturing on the planet, NVIDIA operations chief Deb Shoquist has required three things of every supply chain partner: extreme technical skill, unshakeable trust and a willingness to always try something new. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. items.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. items.fullText: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery November 16, 2026 by Kibibi Moseley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. items.fullText: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing Over two decades, CUDA, the platform that turned GPUs into the engine of modern science, has advanced Nobel Prize-winning research and more. November 16, 2026 by Brett Murray 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI. CUDA’s 20th anniversary presents an occasion to reflect across computing eras, from the people who wrote the very first CUDA programs to the AI developers building on their work today. At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do. From SC06 to SC26 NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 and brought it to the scientific community at SC06, giving scientists and developers a familiar, high-level programming model for using GPUs. It fundamentally extended accelerated computing beyond graphics use cases to accelerate demanding applications for science, simulation and more. In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research , accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films . Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Honoring the Architects of Progress Now, at SC26, NVIDIA is looking back at some of the CUDA luminaries who’ve spearheaded breakthroughs in science and AI: At the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, biophysicist Klaus Schulten’s team helped connect GPU computing with molecular biology through Nanoscale Molecular Dynamics and Visual Molecular Dynamics , tools for molecular simulation and visualization. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing w

items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Contribution and New AI Infrastructure At KubeCon, NVIDIA is putting tools to secure agents and run AI on Kubernetes in the hands of the cloud-native community. November 10, 2026 by Warren Barkley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon , the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell , an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate , an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform : NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine , NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot . These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future. items.fullText: Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation At the Conference on Robot Learning, NVIDIA is introducing GR00T 2, Isaac Lab 3.0 and new open benchmarks, built in collaboration with partners, bringing precision and scale to robot training. November 9, 2026 by Sasa Docca 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Simulation, which has long been the proving ground for robots learning to walk, roll and hop, is now helping researchers teach robots tasks that require a finer touch: aligning gears, connecting cables and assembling small components. The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems. At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing new open robotics technologies, including world action models , simulation tools, benchmarks and agentic workflows. Two NVIDIA papers are among six finalists out of thousands of submissions for the Best Paper Awards at CoRL: GRAIL (Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models), which presents a digital generation pipeline for 3D assets and simulator-ready scenes for robot learning. RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies , which introduces a robot model and training recipe that scales visuomotor context three orders of magnitude beyond state-of-the-art policies without growing inference latency. These advancements help researchers train robots on complex tasks, evaluate their performance across changing conditions and use failures to guide further learning — building the precision, adaptability and autonomy needed to move from lab demonstrations to industrial deployment. NVIDIA is working with partners like Ambi Robotics , Bosch Research , Dexmate , Dyna Robotics , FieldAI , Flexion , Noitom Robotics , Siemens
